General relativity

 Home Physics Branches of physics
OurBigBook.com Words: 43k Articles: 868
General relativity describes gravity through the geometry of spacetime. Its metric tensor specifies distances, proper time measured by clocks, and the causal structure that limits communication. Matter and radiation affect this geometry through the Einstein field equations; freely falling test particles follow geodesics of the resulting geometry. A planet's orbit and a falling apple therefore belong to the same geometric story. The Newtonian limit recovers familiar Newtonian gravity when fields are weak and speeds are small compared with the speed of light. See David Tong's introduction to general relativity.
The most direct way to understand spacetime curvature is to compare neighboring freely falling bodies. Even when each body feels weightless, their separation can change: this is geodesic deviation, observed as a tidal force. Curvature concerns these relative measurements, rather than the shape of a drawing in an imagined surrounding space. A second accessible measurement is gravitational time dilation: identical clocks maintained at different heights accumulate different proper times. Together, tides and clocks turn an abstract geometry into laboratory questions.

Parametrized post-Newtonian formalism (PPN)

Words: 71 Articles: 1
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The parametrized post-Newtonian formalism expresses a weak-field metric tensor using phenomenological parameters so that different gravitational theories can be compared with the same observations. Its spatial-curvature parameter γPPN​ is one in general relativity; it is distinct from the kinematic Lorentz factor.

Parametrized post-Newtonian light deflection (α=2(1+γPPN​)GM/(bc2))

Words: 36
Parametrized post-Newtonian formalism OurBigBook.com
The leading Schwarzschild light deflection of a distant ray passing an isolated spherical mass is α=2(1+γPPN​)GM/(bc2). Thus measurements of angular displacement can constrain γPPN​ rather than merely detect a nonzero gravitational field. In general relativity this becomes the Schwarzschild light deflection 4GM/(bc2).

Synchronous coordinates (ds2=c2dt2−hij​(t,x)dxidxj)

Words: 57
General relativity OurBigBook.com
In synchronous coordinates, fixed spatial-coordinate worldlines are timelike geodesics, and t is their proper time. The metric has unit lapse function and zero shift vector in time units consistent with the displayed factor c2. Indeed gtt​=c2 and gti​=0 give Γμtt​=0. Locally, an irrotational freely falling congruence permits this construction before crossings of the coordinate worldlines. Comoving observers in a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric provide the standard cosmological example.

Gravitational singularity theorem

Words: 13
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A theorem giving conditions under which some geodesic is incomplete. The Penrose singularity theorem is one example.

Israel junction conditions ([hab​]=0,[Kab​]−hab​[K]=−κD2​Sab​)

Words: 73
General relativity OurBigBook.com
Across a thin timelike matter layer, the induced metric is continuous while the jump in its extrinsic curvature is determined by the surface stress-energy tensor. Choose one common spacelike normal and Kab​=21​∂y​hab​ in Gaussian normal coordinates. The singular tangential Einstein tensor is −([Kab​]−hab​[K])δ(y); equating it to κD2​Sab​δ(y) gives the displayed conditions. Reversing the normal or the sign convention for extrinsic curvature changes the corresponding jump signs consistently. These conditions determine the cosmological expansion law of a thin gravitating brane.

Trapping horizon

Words: 70
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A trapping horizon is a hypersurface foliated by marginal two-surfaces with one null expansion zero and the other nonzero. A future outer trapping horizon has θ+​=0, θ−​<0 and Ln​θ+​<0 for a future ingoing null normal n. Unlike an event horizon, this is a quasi-local definition. Under the null energy condition, a regular future outer horizon is spacelike or null. The ingoing derivative condition distinguishes its outer type from an inner trapping horizon.

Congruence (general relativity)

Words: 41
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A congruence in general relativity is a family of curves through an open spacetime region such that each point lies on exactly one member. Its tangent field describes the family locally. A geodesic congruence is the special case in which every member is a geodesic.

Causal structure

Words: 36
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The causal structure of a spacetime classifies separations and tangent directions as timelike, null or spacelike through its light cones. It determines which events can communicate by causal curves. A null curve is one member of this broader geometric structure.

Flat-background scalar-force theory of gravity (dpi=∂iΦpj​dxj−(pj∂j​Φ)dxi)

Words: 168 Articles: 1
General relativity OurBigBook.com
This covariant scalar-force model uses the Minkowski metric and the displayed momentum law, with □Φ=−4πGTii​. For a massive test particle, write pi=mui, uiui​=1. Contracting the force law with pi​ gives constant rest mass; the acceleration is dui/dτ=∂iΦ−ui(uj∂j​Φ), independent of the mass. A static weak field obeys the Poisson equation and yields Newtonian acceleration −∇Φ. For a photon, p⋅dx=0 and dx is parallel to p, so dpi=−pidΦ: photon energies change but their unparametrized paths remain straight. The motion law has the same unparametrized curves as the conformal metric e2Φη, but the field equation must not be silently identified with a different scalar-gravity theory.

Scalar-force gravitational redshift (νr​/νe​=eΦe​−Φr​)

Words: 60
Flat-background scalar-force theory of gravity OurBigBook.com
For a photon in the flat-background scalar-force theory of gravity, eΦpi is constant along its path. In a static field, energies measured by stationary laboratories therefore satisfy the displayed ratio. At first order, Δν/ν=−ΔΦ in units c=1, matching the weak-field Pound-Rebka experiment. This agreement does not imply light bending: a momentum change parallel to the original null tangent changes its scale, not its direction.

Taub–NUT space

Words: 43
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The single-centre Euclidean Taub–NUT geometry is a gravitational instanton with a circle fibre over three-dimensional space. Its fibre shrinks smoothly at the centre when its period is chosen appropriately. Adding flat worldvolume directions gives the local geometry of a Kaluza-Klein monopole.
// Target: algebra.bigb

Near-horizon limit

Words: 147 Articles: 1
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A limit retaining the geometry near a horizon while discarding terms describing its distant asymptotic region. For a regular extremal brane throat, removing the constant from its harmonic function can yield an Anti-de Sitter spacetime factor. Local symmetries and supersymmetries of the limiting geometry need not extend to the full original spacetime.

Rindler limit of a Schwarzschild horizon

Words: 98
Near-horizon limit OurBigBook.com
Outside a Schwarzschild metric horizon rs​, write r−rs​=ρ2/(4rs​). To leading order the radial metric is
ds2≃(2rs​cρ​)2dt2−dρ2.
(1)
It has Rindler coordinates with α=c/(2rs​). The proper-distance-like coordinate ρ has null paths exponential in ±ct/(2rs​); the Schwarzschild coordinate difference r−rs​∝ρ2 is exponential in ±ct/rs​.
Inside, writing rs​−r=ρ2/(4rs​) instead gives ds2≃dρ2−[cρ/(2rs​)]2dt2, where the radial coordinate is timelike. The negative-x Rindler wedge is therefore not the black-hole interior: its time coordinate retains the same causal type as in the positive-x wedge. The flat radial limit does not remove the genuine curvature of the full Schwarzschild spacetime.

Einstein-Maxwell theory

Words: 199 Articles: 2
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The Einstein-Maxwell system couples the metric to an electromagnetic field. In geometrized units its source-free equations are Gab​=8πTabEM​, ∇a​Fab=0 and dF=0, with TabEM​=(Fac​Fb​c−41​gab​Fcd​Fcd)/(4π). Electrovacuum need not have vanishing Ricci tensor, so a Komar integral need not be unchanged between different enclosing surfaces.

Majumdar–Papapetrou solution (ds2=−H−2dt2+H2dx2)

Words: 153 Articles: 1
Einstein-Maxwell theory OurBigBook.com
The four-dimensional Majumdar–Papapetrou solution is a static multi-black-hole Einstein-Maxwell solution with H=1+∑i​Mi​/∣x−xi​∣ and positive geometrized masses Mi​. The electromagnetic potential can be written A=±(H−1−1)dt, with a common sign of charge. Its mass at infinity is ∑i​Mi​. Each distinct centre is an extremal horizon of zero surface gravity rather than a pointlike naked metric singularity.

Equivalence principle

Words: 751 Articles: 10
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The equivalence principle states that gravity couples universally to energy-momentum and that a freely falling local frame removes uniform gravitational acceleration at a point. Tidal curvature remains measurable over a finite region.
Imagine releasing a ball inside a small falling elevator. Relative to the cabin it initially floats, because cabin and ball share the same free fall. The weak equivalence principle says this trajectory is independent of the test particle's composition for identical initial conditions. The Einstein equivalence principle further identifies local nongravitational experiments with those of special relativity. It is a statement about experiments in a local inertial frame, not just equality of two masses.
The word local is essential. Coordinates can make the metric tensor equal to the Minkowski metric and its first derivatives vanish at one event. They generally cannot erase the Riemann curvature tensor, which involves second derivatives. Two separated balls can therefore approach or recede even inside the falling cabin. A sufficiently extended experiment detects these tidal forces; a long observation can accumulate them even when the cabin is small. The equivalence principle does not identify an entire planetary gravitational field with acceleration in flat spacetime. See Tong's discussion of normal coordinates and local equivalence.

Comma-to-semicolon prescription (∂a​ ⟼ ∇a​)

Words: 73

The prescription replaces partial derivatives in flat-spacetime matter equations by the Levi-Civita connection and the Minkowski metric by the curved metric tensor. It implements minimal gravitational coupling and reproduces flat-spacetime physics at a point in a local inertial frame. It is not a unique rule for rearranged higher-derivative equations: commuting partial derivatives before replacement can conceal a Riemann curvature tensor term afterwards. The derivative-order ambiguity in covariant Maxwell potential equations is an explicit example. The equivalence principle removes uniform gravitational acceleration locally but does not erase tidal curvature over a finite experiment.

A coordinate expression that degenerates must be checked to distinguish a removable coordinate failure from a genuinely excluded point of the geometric domain.

Penrose singularity theorem

The Penrose singularity theorem states that a globally hyperbolic spacetime with a noncompact Cauchy hypersurface, a closed trapped surface, and the null convergence condition is future null-geodesically incomplete. Time reversal replaces the trapped surface by an anti-trapped surface and gives past incompleteness.
In his 1965 paper Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities, Roger Penrose used trapped surfaces and global causal structure to address whether nonspherical perturbations could avert a breakdown during gravitational collapse. Quasars supplied the opening astrophysical motivation. The paper used metric signature (+,−,−,−) and a stronger timelike local-energy assumption; the statement above uses the modern null convergence condition.[ref]
For this version, take a smooth connected four-dimensional spacetime with a time orientation. A Cauchy hypersurface meets every inextendible causal curve exactly once; its existence expresses global hyperbolicity. The hypersurface must be noncompact, meaning not compact; this is a global spatial condition, not an assumption about the size of the collapsing body. The null convergence condition is Rab​kakb≥0 for every null vector k. Through the Einstein field equations it follows from the null energy condition; a cosmological constant drops out of the null contraction.[ref]
The conclusion is that at least one future-inextendible null geodesic has a finite upper endpoint of its affine parameter. It neither asserts infinite mass density or divergent curvature at every endpoint, nor says that such an endpoint is visible. Locating an event horizon requires additional global information; the theorem is not a horizon-finding rule for arbitrary spacetimes. Weak cosmic censorship conjecture is an additional issue.[ref]
The supermassive black hole account describes the motivating observational evidence from stellar orbits at the Galactic centre. Such measurements infer a compact gravitating mass. They do not observe a trapped surface, measure a geodesic's complete future, or experimentally prove the Penrose singularity theorem.

(41)
The surface variation is finite under the usual differentiable asymptotic falloff and is not removed by simply taking the boundary to infinity. Adding Arnowitt-Deser-Misner energy cancels it and makes Hamilton's equations well defined for allowed variations that need not fix the energy. On the constraint surface, the total Hamiltonian for that time translation equals the boundary energy.

Bondi news function

Asymptotically flat spacetime

Words: 418 Articles: 6
General relativity OurBigBook.com
An asymptotically flat spacetime approaches Minkowski spacetime sufficiently far from isolated sources. At null infinity this is stated invariantly by requiring a smooth conformal completion whose boundary contains future and past null infinity.

Asymptotic simplicity

Words: 59
Asymptotically flat spacetime OurBigBook.com
Asymptotic simplicity requires a suitable smooth conformal completion with g​=Ω2g, Ω>0 in the physical spacetime, and Ω=0, dΩ=0 on null infinity, such that every inextendible null geodesic has both past and future endpoints there. It is stronger than merely possessing an asymptotically flat exterior. Null geodesics ending on singularities or on omitted finite-affine-distance horizons prevent this global condition.

Conformal completion

Words: 330 Articles: 4
Asymptotically flat spacetime OurBigBook.com
A conformal completion embeds a physical spacetime (M,g) into a manifold with boundary carrying a regular metric gˉ​=Ω2g. Infinity is represented by Ω=0 with dΩ=0; the causal character of each boundary component is determined by gˉ​ab∇ˉa​Ω∇ˉb​Ω.
This spacetime boundary construction is a conformal compactification, not an arbitrary topological compactification.

Minkowski conformal compactification (gˉ​=−dT2+dR2+sin2RdΩ2)

Words: 233 Articles: 2
Conformal completion OurBigBook.com
For four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, set p=arctan((t−r)/L) and q=arctan((t+r)/L), with L>0, then T=p+q, R=q−p. Multiplication by the square of the conformal factor 2cospcosq/L yields the displayed metric on R≥0, ∣T∣+R<π. Its radial Penrose diagram is a triangle: the timelike edge R=0 is the ordinary centre, while the two sloping edges are future null infinity and past null infinity. A signed Cartesian spatial coordinate in two dimensions gives a full diamond instead.
Geodesic endpoints in Minkowski conformal compactification
Words: 81
Minkowski conformal compactification OurBigBook.com
A complete inertial timelike geodesic in Minkowski spacetime has x=b+vt with ∣v∣<1. Under p=arctan(t−r), q=arctan(t+r), both p,q tend to the same endpoint, giving past timelike infinity and future timelike infinity. A complete null geodesic has one finite limiting null coordinate at each end and reaches past null infinity and future null infinity. Complete spacelike geodesics have r>∣t∣ asymptotically and both ends approach spacelike infinity. The endpoints have finite compactified coordinates but occur at infinite physical affine parameter. A conformal transformation preserves null paths as unparametrized geodesics; it does not generally preserve timelike or spacelike geodesic paths.
Projective Minkowski compactification (ML​=(S1×S3)/Z2​)
Words: 84
Minkowski conformal compactification OurBigBook.com
The Lorentzian real form of the Klein quadric is the projectivized real null cone of signature (2,4). Scaling a nonzero null vector makes its positive two-dimensional and negative four-dimensional parts both unit vectors. Real projectivization then identifies (u,v) with (−u,−v), yielding the displayed quotient. Its universal cover is R×S3, and its fundamental group is infinite cyclic. An affine Minkowski chart omits a null cone at infinity. This projective compact space is distinct from an unwrapped causal cover used for a Penrose diagram.

Future null infinity (I+)

Words: 43
Conformal completion OurBigBook.com
Future null infinity is the boundary reached by future-directed outgoing null geodesics in an asymptotically flat spacetime. In four dimensions it has topology R×S2 under the standard asymptotic-flatness assumptions.
It is the future component of null infinity; the past component is I−.

Perfect fluid

Words: 30
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A perfect fluid has no viscosity or heat flux in its local rest frame; its stress is specified by energy density and isotropic pressure. Its relativistic realization is the perfect fluid in general relativity.

Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates

Words: 72 Articles: 1
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The advanced time v=t+r∗​ or retarded time u=t−r∗​ combines Schwarzschild time with the Schwarzschild tortoise coordinate to remove one horizon-coordinate singularity. The advanced choice gives ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates; the retarded choice is outgoing.

Ingoing Kerr-Schild coordinates for Schwarzschild spacetime (t′=t+(2μ/c)log∣r/(2μ)−1∣)

Words: 44
Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates OurBigBook.com
With f=1−2μ/r, the time coordinate t′=t+(2μ/c)log∣r/(2μ)−1∣ gives ds2=fc2dt′2−(4μc/r)dt′dr−(1+2μ/r)dr2−r2dΩ2. Its radial metric tensor block has determinant −c2, so it extends regularly across the future Schwarzschild event horizon. The advanced null time of ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates is v=t′+r/c, not t′ itself. Radial null directions satisfy dr/(cdt′)=−1 or (1−2μ/r)/(1+2μ/r).

Conformally flat manifold

Words: 39
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A (pseudo-)Riemannian manifold is conformally flat if every point has a neighborhood on which the metric is g=Ω2η for a flat metric η and a positive function Ω. This is a local property and does not imply global flatness.

Kerr metric

Words: 36
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The Kerr metric is the stationary axisymmetric vacuum metric of a rotating mass. Parameters M and a determine whether its geometry has the horizons of a Kerr black hole; the metric also admits over-extremal parameters with no horizon.

Ergosphere

Words: 31
General relativity OurBigBook.com
An ergosphere is the region outside a rotating black hole horizon in which the stationary time-translation Killing vector is spacelike. Observers cannot remain stationary relative to infinity there. The Kerr ergoregion is its Kerr-metric instance.
